title: Academic Foundation
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for academic foundation.

items.definition_en: a way of dealing with a subject
items.example: The course uses a practical approach to learning.

items.definition_en: a fact that influences a result
items.example: Cost is an important factor in the decision.

items.definition_en: facts that support a conclusion
items.example: The author provides evidence for the claim.

items.definition_en: an organised way of doing something
items.example: Researchers tested a new method.

title: Education
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for education.

items.definition_en: the subjects taught by a school
items.example: The curriculum includes science and languages.

items.definition_en: something successfully completed
items.example: Graduation was a major achievement.

items.definition_en: the process of judging performance
items.example: The final assessment includes a presentation.

items.definition_en: an ability developed through practice
items.example: Critical thinking is a valuable skill.

title: Environment
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for environment.

items.definition_en: the usual weather conditions of a region
items.example: The region has a dry climate.

items.definition_en: protection of nature and resources
items.example: The project supports forest conservation.

items.definition_en: naturally replaced after use
items.example: Solar power is a renewable energy source.

items.definition_en: the natural home of an animal or plant
items.example: Development threatens the bird's habitat.

title: Health
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for health.

items.definition_en: medical care for an illness
items.example: The patient responded well to treatment.

items.definition_en: to stop something from happening
items.example: Regular exercise can prevent some diseases.

items.definition_en: a physical sign of an illness
items.example: A persistent cough can be a symptom.

items.definition_en: a state of health and happiness
items.example: Sleep affects emotional well-being.

title: Society
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for society.

items.definition_en: people living in or sharing one area
items.example: The centre serves the local community.

items.definition_en: an unfair difference in status or opportunity
items.example: The policy aims to reduce inequality.

items.definition_en: a belief or custom passed between generations
items.example: The festival is an important local tradition.

items.definition_en: someone who works without payment
items.example: Each volunteer received basic training.

title: Cities
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for cities.

items.definition_en: basic systems needed by a society
items.example: The city is investing in transport infrastructure.

items.definition_en: a residential area outside a city centre
items.example: They moved to a quiet suburb.

items.definition_en: overcrowding, especially by traffic
items.example: Cycle lanes may reduce traffic congestion.

items.definition_en: a place provided for a particular purpose
items.example: The neighbourhood has excellent sports facilities.

title: Media
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for media.

items.definition_en: people who watch, read, or listen
items.example: The programme attracts a young audience.

items.definition_en: the title of a news report
items.example: The headline did not reflect the full story.

items.definition_en: a person or place providing information
items.example: Check whether the source is reliable.

items.definition_en: to transmit a programme by television or radio
items.example: The debate was broadcast live.

title: Science
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for science.

items.definition_en: a controlled scientific test
items.example: The experiment produced unexpected results.

items.definition_en: an explanation based on evidence
items.example: Further evidence supports the theory.

items.definition_en: to watch carefully and record
items.example: Scientists observed changes in behaviour.

items.definition_en: something found for the first time
items.example: The discovery changed modern medicine.

title: Work and Economy
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for work and economy.

items.definition_en: paid work or the state of having it
items.example: Employment increased in the service sector.

items.definition_en: money received from work or investment
items.example: Housing costs consume much of their income.

items.definition_en: businesses producing a type of goods or service
items.example: Tourism is a major local industry.

items.definition_en: the rate at which work is completed
items.example: Better equipment improved productivity.

title: Culture
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for culture.

items.definition_en: traditions and history inherited from the past
items.example: The museum protects the region's cultural heritage.

items.definition_en: a traditional way of behaving
items.example: Removing shoes indoors is a common custom.

items.definition_en: the qualities that define a person or group
items.example: Language can shape cultural identity.

items.definition_en: including many different types or people
items.example: The city has a diverse population.

title: Crime and Law Basics
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for crime and law basics.

items.definition_en: an act that breaks the law
items.example: Driving without a licence is an offence.

items.definition_en: a person harmed by a crime
items.example: The service provides support to each victim.

items.definition_en: to examine facts to discover the truth
items.example: Police are investigating the incident.

items.definition_en: a punishment ordered by a court
items.example: The judge imposed a short sentence.

title: Common Academic Verbs
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for common academic verbs.

items.definition_en: to examine something in detail
items.example: The essay analyses two possible causes.

items.definition_en: to show that something exists or is likely
items.example: The data indicates a steady increase.

items.definition_en: to examine similarities and differences
items.example: The study compares urban and rural schools.

items.definition_en: to judge quality or effectiveness
items.example: We need to evaluate the available evidence.

title: Adjective–Noun Collocations
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for adjective–noun collocations.

items.definition_en: an important or noticeable difference
items.example: The survey shows a significant change in attitudes.

items.definition_en: a problem of considerable importance
items.example: Housing remains a major issue.

items.definition_en: facts that clearly support a conclusion
items.example: There is strong evidence for the link.

items.definition_en: a large variety of things
items.example: The library offers a wide range of resources.

title: Verb–Noun Collocations
description: Build accurate, usable vocabulary for verb–noun collocations.

items.definition_en: to decide what evidence means
items.example: The researchers reached a cautious conclusion.

items.definition_en: to increase public knowledge
items.example: The campaign raises awareness of road safety.

items.definition_en: to provide what is required
items.example: The programme meets a clear community need.

items.definition_en: to do something practical about a problem
items.example: Local authorities must take action quickly.
